videos.title: Flaky Tests: How to Tell a Real Bug From a Guess (With AI)06 lesson flaky test autopsy WEB
videos.description:
#FlakyTests  #TestAutomation  #SoftwareTesting

Forty tests failed overnight. Two are real bugs. This is how to tell which
two — and what to do with the other thirty-eight — without just hitting
rerun and hoping.

This is the direct follow-up to Lesson 01 (AI in Software Testing). Same
format: animated, no hype, built around a real-looking regression suite
taken apart on screen. It covers what "flaky" actually means, the six most
common causes ranked by how often they show up, how to use AI to rank
causes with evidence instead of guessing, and the guardrails that stop
"just add a retry" from quietly hiding a real bug.

No prior AI knowledge assumed. If you've ever stared at a red CI build and
hit rerun, this one's for you.

⏱️ CHAPTERS
00:00  What this lesson covers
00:54  What flaky actually means
02:55  Meet the suite
03:39  Diagnosing with evidence
06:04  Fixing it, not silencing it
08:12  The guardrails
09:12  How to start this month

🔍 WHAT'S COVERED
The actual definition of flaky — same code, same input, different result
The six most common causes, ranked by how often they show up
The triage loop: reproduce, isolate, rank — with evidence at every step
The exact prompt that replaces a guess with a ranked, evidenced answer
Clustering failures by root cause instead of triaging test by test
Band-aid fixes versus real cures, matched cause by cause
Quarantine done properly — an owner and an expiry date on every row
Five guardrails, including an auditable quarantine.yaml

💬 THE LINE TO REMEMBER
"It's not thirty-eight flaky tests. It's one shared login helper leaving a
session behind."

That's the whole payoff of ranking causes with evidence instead of
re-running and hoping — forty separate-looking problems are often two or
three, once you can see the shared cause.

👤 ABOUT
I'm Ronak. I run QA and I administer the databases underneath it, so
everything here is filtered through the same two questions: does it find
real defects, and does it stay away from production data?

🔔 Subscribe — next lesson, an AI is writing SQL straight at your database.
Here's the DBA's survival guide.

📌 The quarantine.yaml block from 08:51 is pinned in the comments.

videos.title: FlakeWarden: Agentic Flaky-Test Triage on UiPath Test Cloud (AgentHack 2026 Winner)
videos.description:
FlakeWarden is an agent that triages failing tests on UiPath Test Cloud. When a build goes red, it decides whether each failure is a real defect, a flaky test, or an environment issue, then routes it to the right action with a human approving anything that changes. Clear-cut cases are settled by exact, auditable math; only the genuinely ambiguous failures reach a grounded Agent Builder classifier.

This is the demo from my UiPath AgentHack 2026 submission, where FlakeWarden won 1st place in the Test Cloud track. It was built for the hackathon, so the live deployment may not be running right now.

How it works:
A deterministic flake-scorer (five statistics over run history) handles the confident cases with no AI
A grounded classifier in UiPath Agent Builder reasons over the ambiguous ones (stack trace, selector diff, commit, logs)
UiPath Maestro orchestrates the flow, Action Center is the human approval gate, and Orchestrator writes the result back
Built end to end with a coding agent (Claude Code driving the uip CLI)

Measured results (on a synthetic-but-adversarial corpus of 150 labeled failures):
90.7% overall accuracy
0% safety-direction false-positive rate (a real regression is never hidden as flaky)
About a third of failures resolved by exact math, with no model call

Links:
Write-up: https://jonathanandrei.com/blog/flake...
Code (GitHub, MIT): https://github.com/JonathanSolvesProb...
Slide deck (PDF): https://jonathanandrei.com/decks/flak...

The "16% of tests flaky / 84% of red builds" figure is from J. Micco, "Flaky Tests at Google and How We Mitigate Them" (Google Testing Blog, 2016).

videos.title: ChronoTrace — an AI agent that isn't allowed to cheat at fixing flaky tests
videos.description:
ChronoTrace is an autonomous agent that repairs concurrency-induced flaky tests in Python
asyncio code, and proves the repair worked — built on the AWS Strands Agents SDK and
Amazon Bedrock for the Agents for Humans Hackathon.

The problem: a test that passes on rerun without a code change. At Google, 84% of
post-submit CI failures are flaky tests rather than real bugs. Microsoft measured
flakiness costing $1.14M a year.

Most AI coding assistants "fix" these by inserting a sleep or a retry. The test goes
green, the race is still live, and CI is permanently slower. ChronoTrace cannot do that:

• A 15-rule deterministic AST governor rejects sleeps, aliased sleep imports, retry
  decorators, timeout inflation, weakened assertions and no-op patches — 17 adversarial
  attacks, 17 rejections, each by the rule that targets it.
• The model (Amazon Nova Pro / Nova Lite) emits a typed RepairIntent, never raw code.
• Forced replay gates coroutine entry to reproduce the exact failing interleaving, so
  "fixed the race" and "made it rarer" cannot be confused.

Act II is the part worth watching: our own agent proposes a patch that breaks no rule,
passes the policy gate 15/15 — and is still wrong. Forced replay catches it. A
rerun-based gate reads the same patch as a 75%-to-70% improvement and ships it.

Chapters
0:00 A failing test, 20 runs
0:18 What a flaky test actually is
0:58 What everyone else does about it
1:27 How ChronoTrace works
2:06 Act I — a race, repaired and proven
2:39 The governor gauntlet

videos.title: Flaky Test Detective — Evidence-Driven CI Reliability | Ready, Spec, Ship Hackathon
videos.description:
Flaky Test Detective is an evidence-driven CI reliability tool that separates flaky tests from genuine regressions using historical JUnit test results.

Instead of guessing from error messages, it looks for measurable evidence such as same-commit divergence — the same test passing and failing against identical code.

It can:

distinguish flaky tests from real regressions and consistently broken tests
identify flakiness introduced by a branch versus inherited flakiness
correlate failures with execution environments
experimentally reproduce order-dependent flakes using delta debugging
verify whether a flaky-test fix actually worked
provide a local dashboard, CLI, GitHub Action, and standalone reports

The detector was also validated against real open-source software using the IDoFT flaky-test research dataset:

12 open-source repositories
288 suite runs
41,585 test executions
99.4% recall among labelled flakes that reproduced
183/183 flagged tests backed by observed same-commit divergence
0 consistently failing tests incorrectly dismissed as flaky

Real-world testing also exposed a major weakness in the original design: historical order-dependence diagnosis dropped to only 11.6% on real repositories. Rather than hiding the result, the project published it and evolved toward controlled reproduction experiments.

Flaky Test Detective was built for the Ready, Spec, Ship Hackathon using Kiro through four iterative specification rounds:

Initial detector
Accuracy & adoption
Product layer
Investigation engine

Each round was driven by measurements, failed assumptions, ADRs, and the findings from the previous implementation.
Built with Kiro for Ready, Spec, Ship 2026.

videos.title: Debug Flaky Hardware Tests Without Hiding Real Bugs
videos.description:
Debug flaky hardware tests without hiding a real bug. The checked example separates product failure, test defect, lab error, wrong device, and fail-then-pass in plain English.

Its main rule is simple: a passing retry does not erase the first failure. Every attempt keeps its own identity and evidence. A third uncontrolled attempt is rejected.

You will learn:

why the same timeout can have very different causes
what to save before reset or cleanup changes the scene
how requirement and oracle versions reveal test defects
why identity and lab health gates come before product judgment
how two healthy rigs strengthen product-failure evidence
why fail then pass means `FLAKY_OBSERVED`
how a small reproduction budget stops green-result searching
how to prove a repair without losing the original failure

The included values are fixed demo observations. No real board, rig, or network is used.

Chapters:
00:00 A passing retry does not erase the failure that came before it
00:24 Save the first bad run before reset, cleanup, or another attempt changes the scene
00:59 Read the device and active build before blaming either test or product
01:32 Every reproduction must be a new attempt linked to the same investigation
02:07 A broken health check or unstable link blocks a product verdict
02:39 A useful reproduction changes one planned variable or confirms the same setup
03:12 The code proves five result paths and a strict reproduction limit
03:35 A flaky result now becomes a clear investigation instead of a hidden failure

videos.title: Module 18: Testing - Confidence, Not Coverage
videos.description:
Visit https://shipreal.dev for the full course 🚀

This module rebuilds your testing strategy around one question: does this test catch a real bug, or just prove code ran? You'll learn to write the behavior sentence before the test and delete tests that break during safe refactors, size your suite by where complexity actually lives (domain logic pulls weight toward unit tests, glue-heavy apps push it toward integration tests against a real containerized database), and double only at process boundaries using fakes over mocks with outcome-based assertions. You'll also pick up property-based testing to find inputs you'd never think to type, contract testing to catch breaking API changes before customers do, and mutation testing to get an honest score instead of a coverage percentage that counts executed lines but not verified behavior. By the end you'll know how to review AI-generated tests for real assertions, set a flaky test policy with actual deadlines, and decide when TDD earns its keep as a design tool instead of a ritual.
